notes:
Original title verified against supplied reference. Explicit Study 2a and p. 8 locator identify the elderly-priming walking-time test. Cached OCR prints degrees of freedom as 2S; t value and p bound are legible. N=30 is explicitly the Experiment 2a participant sample; no exclusions are described and the target test is presented for that experiment. Replication independently attempted through permitted open-access routes; no full text obtained. No narrative replication verdict extracted from abstract/preview. Acquisition details: /home/lukas/.t3/worktrees/fred-data/audit-fred-stats-2026-10/audit/fred_stats_2026-10/texts/15b44d22cd172bf5d7c91d46.miss The neutral description is generic; target selected using explicit original study and page locator, not assumed to describe a different test.
Source follow-up: Published article title, authors and DOI match the supplied replication reference. Extracted the elderly-versus-neutral prime main effect corresponding to the original walking-speed effect, rather than the self-consciousness interaction. No unambiguous standalone author replication-success category is assigned to this individual study; the authors explicitly claim replication only for combined Studies 1a/1b analyses, so reported_success remains null rather than inferring a verdict from p. The separately printed interaction is F(1, 36) = 6.77, p = .01. The reported residual df of 36 is retained but was not used to manufacture a separately printed final n. Combined analyses have residual df 60 and report prime-group Ns of 36 and 32, so these pooled sample counts cannot resolve the separate-study final n. Original side is an unassigned placeholder and was not consulted. Source version: published article supplied by licensed EBSCO PsycInfo service.
